question_text: What disease would we suspect in a young patient who reported a frequent history of dysphagia to solids and liquids with impaired food repeated, without clinical symptoms of pyrosis and in which multiple oral esophageal rings with normal mucosa (trachealized appearance) are observed in oral endoscopy?

Question: What disease would we suspect in a young patient who reported a frequent history of dysphagia to solids and liquids with impaired food repeated, without clinical symptoms of pyrosis and in which multiple oral esophageal rings with normal mucosa (trachealized appearance) are observed in oral endoscopy?

Options:
opa. Herpetic esophagitis.
opb. Eosinophilic esophagitis.
opc. Candidiasic esophagitis.
opd. Cytomegalovirus esophagitis.
ope. Adenocarcinoma of the esophagus.
